text:
sam: Heads-up — console alerts for streaming reconnects spiked ~12:34 UTC, ~500 events in 2m for tenant-42. Anyone seen this?
opsbot: alert: [streaming.reconnect.rate] 500 events (2m) tenant=tenant-42 route=/sse/subscribe
tara: I saw the dashboard jump too. Time-series shows a sharp pulse at 12:34, coincides with a rollout.
mike: Which rollout? console shows "resume-policy v2" was rolled at 12:30 via canary->all.
anne: Could be sampling/reporting — I think trace-id sampling is different between proxy and ingest tiers, we may be double-counting.
sam: Quick repro: started a debug client with a stale resume token, disconnected, reconnected in a tight loop. Our proxy labels had trace_id X but proxy-forwarded header changed to X' causing duplicate ingestion.
mike: Do we have example logs?
sam: paste:
```
proxy.log 12:34:11 INFO conn_id=abc resume_token=tok123 trace_id=trace-9 forward_id=trace-9
ingest.log 12:34:11 INFO tenant=42 route=/sse/subscribe trace_id=trace-9 sample=1
proxy.log 12:34:12 INFO conn_id=abc reconnect attempt=1 trace_id=trace-10 forward_id=trace-10
ingest.log 12:34:12 INFO tenant=42 route=/sse/subscribe trace_id=trace-10 sample=1
```
tara: So the proxy is rewriting trace_id across reconnect, both events get sampled and counted as separate incidents.
anne: Are we double-billing? Billing metrics come from ingestion; if the same logical session churns and gets counted twice we may have overcharge.
mike: Could routing policy cause client to hit multiple ingest shards and each sample independently?
sam: Yes — sticky routing TTL is 30s, client reattach within 3s but hit a different shard because cookie expired at edge. Two shards both sample at 1/100 so chance both picked it.
tara: Quick mitigation: lower sampling rate OR dedupe on resume_id in ingestion before emitting alert. Which is lower effort?
anne: Dedupe is safe: ingest can dedupe by resume_id within 10s window. Low risk but needs small cache.
mike: Alternative: preserve an opaque session_id from proxy that survives reconnect so ingest sees same id. Proxy change is heavier.
sam: Small patch idea:
```
# proxy: on reconnect if client provides old session_id -> reuse it
session_id = client.session_id or generate()
forward header X-Session-ID: session_id
```
opsbot: deploy: canary resume-policy v2 -> 12:30 by mike (done)
tara: If we roll back, we'll lose the new sticky behavior. I'd rather fix ingest dedupe for alerts quickly.
anne: I'll open a hotfix PR for ingest dedupe and add a 15s in-memory cache keyed by resume_id. Low risk.
mike: I'll add a console alert suppression: if same resume_id emitted within 15s, collapse to single alert (UI-side).
sam: Can someone verify no billing delta for last hour? @finance (not on thread)
opsbot: note: rolling back canary to resume-policy v1 requires db migration revert; rollback ETA 45m
tara: Filed PRs: ingest hotfix #824 (waiting CI), console collapse #825, proxy sticky session ticket #826
anne: I'll prod CI — if green, I'll merge and push to canary-only first.
mike: Also add telemetry tag "session.tenancy=resume_id" so we can trace dedupe effectiveness.
sam: Great. After hotfix, let's monitor for 30m and then reopen billing-sampling if needed. :thumbsup:
